items.title: Before you buy another USB-C charger, make sure it has this critical (and hidden) spec
items.summary: Buying a USB-C charger is still harder than it should be.
items.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Buying the perfect USB-C charger may look simple at first, but the reality is full of potential gotchas. If you’ve ever reached for your cable only to find that your device is still charging hours later, you’re certainly not alone. In one sense, USB-C and USB Power Delivery were supposed to solve this mess. The universal connector and new regulations, such as those introduced in the EU, were designed to ensure that one charger could support everything. In some ways, that has been a success: USB-C can now be found on almost every phone, tablet, laptop, and more. However, the difference between something that technically works and something that works optimally can still be surprisingly wide.

items.summary: مزاعم جديدة تهز عرش جياني
items.body: مزاعم جديدة تهز عرش جياني يواجه جياني إنفانتينو، رئيس الاتحاد الدولي لكرة القدم (فيفا)، ضغوطًا جديدة تهدد بإشعال الجدل حول مستقبله في منصبه، بعدما كشف تحقيق صحفي عن دفع الاتحاد الأوروبي لكرة القدم (يويفا) مبلغًا ماليًا من ستة أرقام لامرأة قيل إنها كانت على علاقة بالمسؤول السويسري خلال فترة عمله أمينًا عامًا للاتحاد القاري. وكشفت صحيفة "ديلي تلجراف" البريطانية أن اليويفا دفع المبلغ للمرأة عند انتهاء علاقتها المهنية بالاتحاد، في واقعة تعود إلى الفترة التي كان فيها إنفانتينو يشغل منصب الأمين العام للاتحاد الأوروبي لكرة القدم، بين عامي 2009 و2016. ونقلت الصحيفة عن متحدث باسم إنفانتينو، الذي يشغل حاليًا منصب رئيس الفيفا، قوله إن المسؤول السويسري "ينفي بشدة هذه المزاعم التي لا أساس لها من الصحة على الإطلاق". وأضاف متحدث باسم الفيفا، في تصريحات نقلتها "ديلي تلجراف ": "ينفي رئيس الفيفا جياني إنفانتينو هذه المزاعم بشدة، فهي عارية تمامًا عن الصحة. وأي تلميح بوجود سلوك غير لائق أو انتهاك للأنظمة أو اللوائح يُعد تشهيرًا". وتابع: "لم يسبق لأي موظف في اليويفا أو الفيفا أن تقدم بشكوى تتعلق بسلوك السيد إنفانتينو؛ لأنه لم تكن هناك أي واقعة تورط فيها". اليويفا يؤكد دفع مبلغ مالي من جانبه، أصدر الاتحاد الأوروبي لكرة القدم بيانًا أكد فيه أنه "تم دفع مبلغ مالي للشخص المعني عند إنهاء العلاقة المهنية". …

items.body: The Google Pixel 11 series is nearly here, and a massive leak just a few days ago pretty much revealed all the important bits we’ve been dying to know. The Pixel 11 Pro series will once again shine the brightest, quite literally this time, with the new HiLight notification light . But there doesn’t seem to be much in store for the base Pixel 11, which begs the question — should you simply grab the Pixel 10 at a discount today?

items.title: Forget Recorder — Google’s working on a new AI-powered voice notes tool
items.summary: Conversation Capture is coming.
items.body: TL;DR Android Authority has reviewed strings related to a new Pixel feature called Conversation Capture. Conversation Capture will record and transcribe audio, and with optional Gemini integration. We expect this feature will debut on the Pixel 11 series. One of Google’s best machine-learning enabled products has long been its Pixel-exclusive Recorder app, which makes searchable transcriptions of your recordings. Now, Google is integrating that basic concept deeper into the Android experience with a feature called Conversation Capture. Poking around the latest version of the Android System Intelligence app , we’ve seen a whole bunch of strings about Conversation Capture. items.title: August’s Android Canary release gets app handles and new Quick Settings layout editor
items.summary: Sadly, it's also the end of the line for Pixel 6 phones.
items.body: TL;DR Google’s latest Android Canary build is now out, supporting Pixel 6 and newer hardware. This will be the final Android Canary release for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro. Today’s 2608 build introduces some new ways to customize Quick Settings. Google’s got tons of options right now for testers looking to get a taste of Android’s latest changes before anybody else, but you absolutely need to be first in line, there’s no better option than the Android Canary program. It’s been exactly one month since the 2607 July build arrived, and Google is now back with August’s Android Canary 2608. Over on Reddit’s Canary sub, Google shares the news of Android Canary 2608’s availability. Sadly, it’s not all good, and we’ve got some bad news for testers hoping to eke a little more life out of some of Google’s oldest hardware: Just like Android 17 QPR2 , Canary is also dropping support for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro . The good news is that you can still install today’s release — but that’s it; you’re cut off, going forward.

items.title: OpenAI just made ChatGPT’s latest model more accessible to non-paying users
items.summary: Free users are getting unlimited chats and deeper thinking.
items.body: TL;DR OpenAI’s latest ChatGPT update brings meaningful upgrades to the GPT-5.6 lineup. The top-tier GPT-5.6 Sol model will now make fewer factual errors, limit unnecessary information, and can adapt its reasoning based on your query. Free users are moving from GPT-5.5 Instant to GPT-5.6 Luna with unlimited text chats and a new Think button for deeper reasoning. ChatGPT’s latest 5.6 model lineup made its official debut early in July. Less than a month later, the AI giant is already giving the state-of-the-art models a brain and accessibility boost. As you may recall, the 5.6 series consists of three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. There’s no update to Terra, but GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna are getting meaningful upgrades . These range from making the models more reliable, accurate, and focused, to expanding access for users who don’t want to pay for top-tier AI.

items.title: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
items.summary: The gloves are off as GrapheneOS calls Revolut's approach to security "incredibly negligent."
items.body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS says some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app. The project claims Revolut is specifically targeting GrapheneOS while still supporting outdated Android versions. GrapheneOS suggests a possible workaround but warns that it may not continue to work in the long term. Banking apps can be suspicious of anything that strays from the standard Android experience, but GrapheneOS clearly believes Revolut is taking that distrust way too far. The privacy-focused Android project claims some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app, accusing the fintech company of deliberately trying to shut them out. In a thread on X , GrapheneOS said Revolut is blaming the restriction on security concerns, but argued that the real issue is that they’re enforcing licensing on Google Play . It also questioned how strict Revolut’s security standards can really be when the app still supports Android 9, which launched back in 2018. It went further, describing Revolut as “incredibly negligent when it comes to security.”

With less than a week to go until August 12 , we are in full Pixel 11 anticipation mode, looking forward to all the hardware getting set to debut at the next Made by Google event. Lately, we’ve been captivated not just by Pixel 11 leak after Pixel 11 leak , but also Google starting to whet our appetite with a few official teasers . Today it takes those to the next level with a look at not just what , but who we can look forward to at the event itself. As you may remember from last summer, Jimmy Fallon hosted the Pixel 10 launch , joined by celebs like the NBA’s Stephen Curry, Formula 1’s Lando Norris, and the Jonas Brothers. And for the Pixel 11 launch, Google sure looks like its getting ready to turn that celebrity dial up to 11.

items.title: Maybe the FCC was onto something: These routers are phoning home to China with a secret backdoor
items.summary: Of course, because they predate the ban, the FCC continues to permit their sale.
items.body: TL;DR A new report details a massive security flaw in Zbtlink-made routers. The routers are programmed to ping a hard-coded list of servers, traced back to China. Once connected, the routers grant full root access — no authentication required. This past spring, the FCC announced a sweeping ban on new foreign-made routers — like the kind you use to get online with your ISP and connect all your devices to Wi-Fi. This was all done in the name of national security, but just how real of a threat do routers pose? The discovery of a new security vulnerability in some Chinese-made routers may have you looking at the FCC’s action in a slightly more sympathetic light. Jacob Baines at VulnCheck shares his analysis of routers made by Zbtlink, sold under both that and Wiflyer branding. While neither are huge names in the router space, they’re still sold through US retailers like Amazon , and have been around for years — so, plenty of time for these devices to make some inroads on the market.

items.title: Google’s making it easier to get to Gemini from Chrome on Android
items.summary: Look, it's Gemini again.
items.body: TL;DR Chrome on Android is testing a new toolbar that provides quick access to Gemini. The new toolbar is rolling out to some users now. Google’s testing another way to remind you that Gemini exists. New controls are appearing in the Chrome browser on Android, adding a button to call up Google’s AI right within thumb’s reach. As reported by 9to5Google , some users (including 9to5′ s Ben Schoon) have started receiving an update to Chrome that introduces a second strip of buttons to the browser UI. By default, this version of Chrome has a URL field, as well as a back button, share button, and and menu button, at the top of the screen, plus a second bar with a Gemini icon and tab controls at the bottom. Tapping the Gemini icon opens a conversation with Google’s AI chatbot.

items.title: Stop jumping between Adobe apps with this new ChatGPT plugin
items.summary: Adobe’s entire creative suite is now in ChatGPT.
items.body: TL;DR After bringing Photoshop, Express, and Acrobat to ChatGPT, Adobe is now launching a unified plugin that brings more than 70 tools under one roof. Users can perform multiple actions, including photo editing, video creation, and more with a single prompt. The new plugin is rolling out globally. It is only available on the web and the desktop app for now. As AI tools become more prevalent, traditional ways of doing things are slowly fading away. You used to perform a Google search for general queries, but now you ask ChatGPT for the same information. Similarly, instead of browsing through multiple websites to plan a trip, you simply ask Gemini to take the reins. AI is clearly changing the way people interact with software and devices, and the latest example of this shift comes in the form of a new Adobe plugin for ChatGPT. For reference, this isn’t Adobe making its ChatGPT debut. The software-maker made Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Express, and Adobe Acrobat accessible within ChatGPT back in December last year. Today’s update significantly expands on that integration.

items.title: Google reveals how much free space Chrome wants to install local AI models
items.summary: It's kind of a lot.
items.body: TL;DR Google has updated its support documentation to show that downloading the models that power Chrome’s on-device AI features requires approximately 20 gigabytes of available storage space. The install size of the models is still approximately 4 GB, Google has confirmed. You can disable Chrome’s on-device AI features in the browser’s settings. Google’s been working for a while to integrate Gemini more deeply into Chrome for some time now. Some users were confused and annoyed this spring when Chrome started automatically downloading a multi-gigabyte file called weights.bin that enables Gemini Nano features to run locally. Now, Google’s updated its documentation to reflect that you’ll actually need quite a bit more free space to actually download the files required for local AI features. As spotted by Windows Report (via PiunikaWeb ), the Google Chrome Help Center entry about the browser’s on-device generative AI models has been updated to reflect that you’ll need approximately 20 gigs of free disk space to install the models that power local AI features. You’ll also need an unmetered data connection, plus “ Sufficient device performance.”

items.title: Google Search patches bug that broke time filters
items.summary: The widespread bug that ignored selected date ranges has now been resolved.
items.body: TL;DR Google has fixed the Search time filter bug that ignored selected date ranges. A Google Search VP confirmed the fix shipped earlier this week. If time filters are still broken, Google is asking users to report it. Good news for anyone who spent the past few days struggling to find recent news or software updates: Google has finally fixed its broken Search time filter feature. We recently reported that Google Search’s time filters — such as “Past 24 hours,” “Past month,” or custom date ranges — had stopped working globally. Instead of isolating results to your chosen timeframe, Search returned a random mix of old and new content, forcing users to rely on manual search operators as a workaround.

items.title: Google Wallet now lets kids tap to pay without giving up parental control
items.summary: Your child gets tap to pay, but not a free pass to overspend.
items.body: TL;DR Google Wallet now supports supervised balances for kids and teens under 18 in the US, giving them a way to make digital payments with parental oversight. Parents can set daily spending limits, view transaction history, receive Family Link purchase alerts, and remotely lock the Wallet if a device is lost. Kids can tap to pay using their Android phone or Wear OS smartwatch anywhere Google Pay is accepted. Giving kids money has always involved a bit of trust. Maybe it’s cash for a weekend outing, a card for an emergency, or money to grab something while they’re out with friends. The problem is that cash is easy to lose, cards can go missing, and it’s not always obvious where the money ended up. That’s exactly the problem Google Wallet is now trying to solve. The company is rolling out supervised Google Wallet balances for children and teenagers under 18 in the US. Instead of handing your child a debit card and simply hoping they spend responsibly, you’ll be able to decide how much money they have access to while still keeping an eye on where it’s going. It’s a much more practical way to let kids start managing their own money without throwing them in at the deep end.

items.title: Mysterious new Garmin smartwatch spotted in FCC filings

items.body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR A new Garmin smartwatch has been spotted in an FCC filing. The device carries the model number A05170 and has support for LTE and satellite connectivity. It also features 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, ANT/ANT+, and NFC. Now that the Cirqa Smart Band is out, you may be wondering what else Garmin is working on. This will come as a surprise, but it turns out that the company’s next product will be a smartwatch. I know, I know, no one could’ve seen that coming. This smartwatch was recently spotted in a regulatory filing. The folks over at Gadgets and Wearables found the filing sitting in the FCC’s database. These documents don’t include the name of the device, but they do reveal that the model number is A05170. Additionally, Garmin describes the hardware as a portable digital transceiver, but the SAR evaluation report calls it a wrist-worn device.

items.title: The Pixel 11 hasn’t even arrived yet, but the majority of you are already against buying it

We’re expecting four phones, plenty of new software tricks, and perhaps a few surprises that haven’t already escaped through the usual leak-shaped holes. Despite all that, it seems most of our readers don’t currently have solid plans to buy one. How do we know this? Well, we ran a poll in a r ecent opinion piece by my colleague Joe Maring, who explained why the Motorola Razr Fold has him questioning his long-standing Pixel loyalty. His argument focused on the Motorola foldable’s cameras, performance, battery life, and charging, but the question we put to you wasn’t related to whether you agreed with his comparisons. We asked more broadly, do you plan on getting any of the new Pixel 11 phones? They haven’t launched yet, so the question was really around your position based on leaks and propensity to upgrade.

items.title: Survey confirms your Fold 8 preference aligns with Samsung pre-orders
items.summary: We need more square phones.
items.body: Samsung’s latest foldable lineup is a departure from what the company’s been doing up to now. Rather than the usual two foldables — a Flip and a Fold — Samsung’s released three, including two book-style Z Fold phones in different aspect ratios. People have seemed excited about the new, wider form factor (the marginally less premium of the two) since before the phones were released , and now a survey Android Authority ‘s been running has confirmed that vibe. In a poll we’ve been running since late July, we asked readers which of the two Z Fold 8 phones they’d be more likely to buy. There were four options: the wide Z Fold 8; the narrow, higher-end Z Fold 8 Ultra; a response for people who hadn’t decided yet; and one for folks who just aren’t interested. After more than 1,000 responses, the wide Z Fold 8 ran away with it, nabbing nearly 60% of all votes.

items.title: DeepSeek is preparing users for a big price hike
items.summary: DeepSeek has reportedly advised clients to plan for an unspecified hike to its API rates in the future.
items.body: TL;DR DeepSeek has reportedly sent out notices to its clients about an upcoming price hike. This means DeepSeek’s current position as the most cost-effective AI service in the business may be short-lived. Notably, this is separate from a mid-July price increase announced by the company for peak-hour usage to ease server loads. Among AI providers like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, China-based DeepSeek has emerged as a more economical option for many. The company earned some positive headlines recently following the launch of its powerful V4 Flash model. Well, there’s some bad news coming today, as DeepSeek is seemingly planning a price hike. According to a report by Bloomberg , DeepSeek is sending notices to its clients, informing them of a “significant” price increase. There’s no word on how much more expensive its offerings will be, nor on when the updated prices will take effect. The general idea behind the notice was to give users enough time to prepare for the imminent changes.

items.title: I won’t ever leave the country without the Timekettle X1 Meeting Interpreter Hub translator
items.summary: Jump over any language barrier with this business-tier translation hub.
items.body: It is said that the Tower of Babel signified the limitless capabilities of human unity and ambition. Truly, language is one of the biggest barriers, but modern technology is breaking it down. AI, translation apps, and certain devices are more accessible and easy to use than ever. Enter the Timekettle X1 Meeting, a device that promises to make multi-language meetings and general translation simple, even when offline. I’ve seen Timekettle translators for some years, usually at technology conventions like CES, which is a pretty good place for them, given the usual mass of multilingual attendees at such events. I always wondered how well they worked outside of such showcases; testing them for a few minutes on the show floor certainly isn’t enough to form an opinion.

items.title: Did the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease get worse after a couple of weeks?

The tipster claimed that the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease got worse after less than two weeks of use. We can also confirm that the Ultra phone’s crease is more pronounced, but that it still feels the same. items.title: Signal finally makes using multiple Android devices much easier
items.summary: You no longer have to choose which phone gets to keep your Signal chats.
items.body: TL;DR Signal now lets you link another Android phone or tablet to your existing account. You can optionally transfer your message history and the last 45 days of media. The update also redesigns Android tablet and foldable layout, ditching legacy single-screen navigation. For years, one of Signal’s biggest pain points when compared to other messaging apps wasn’t encryption, voice calls, or missing features. It was the awkward experience of moving between devices. If you wanted to use a second Android phone or tablet, you were largely out of luck. That finally changes with the latest update.
